title: segresearch: where byte-level language models should start their patches
description:
Code, logs and results for the paper Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses. Byte-level language models such as BLT start a patch where next-byte entropy is high; under tight budgets this skips positions whose type is predictable but whose value must be computed, such as the number after '=' in a worked math solution. The repository contains the BLT-style training harness (MLX, and a PyTorch port verified against it), the experiments on Meta's BLT-1B (with the upstream fix for the 512-byte attention window of the Hugging Face conversion), the scaling study at 1M-50M parameters, the results registry with per-target outputs, and the scripts that regenerate every table, figure and tested number of the paper.

Datasets (GSM8K, MATH, OpenWebMath) and the BLT-1B weights are not redistributed; the scripts download them from their sources.
